title: ‘I told it to never call me again’: AI bots wreak havoc with UK restaurant bookings
summary: Meta claims its Muse assistant will make users’ lives easier, but business owners say AI is driving them to go analogue Restaurant owners are battling a horde of AI bots and returning to using the telephone instead of online booking as new virtual assistants launch in the UK – but sometimes even that isn’t enough to stop them. This week, Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta launched its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it shop and make restaurant reservations. The bot is given access to the user’s email if they give it permission, and it can make restaurant bookings and go shopping on the user’s behalf. Continue reading...

title: La succession: France’s wealthiest family said to be battling over who will take over LVMH
summary: Bernard Arnault’s children – described as ‘modern-day French royals’ – are subject of rivalry rumours over who will succeed him They are France’s richest family, leading the world’s biggest luxury goods empire, dressed in matching Dior suits – a clan so powerful they have been described as modern-day French royals. But in recent months, the family dynasty of Bernard Arnault , 77, the billionaire head of the LVMH group whose brands range from Louis Vuitton handbags to Tiffany jewellery, has become the subject of speculation about internal rivalry over which of his children could take over the company. Continue reading...

title: Stunted sprouts: heatwaves and drought take toll on festive vegetable
summary: The Christmas staple is smaller this year after a hot, dry summer hit the water-loving – but versatile – brassica They are a key ingredient in many Christmas dinners, but brussels sprouts appearing on diners’ plates this festive season are likely to be smaller than usual, after the hot, dry summer took its toll on the water-loving crop. Sprouts are generally planted outdoors between March and early June, meaning they were already in the ground when the UK faced a series of heatwaves and drought conditions across Wales and most of England. title: ‘The key is pricing realistically’: how to sell your home in a falling market
summary: From small fixes such as decluttering to taking your property off the market for a break, there are ways to seal the deal Selling your home is always a big task, but when the headlines are telling you prices are falling, it can feel even more daunting. Average house prices in the UK fell by 1.2% over the year to 31 October, according to Lloyds bank – the steepest drop since late 2023. Continue reading...
